issues.sym: Coolant disappears with no obvious puddle, a sweet smell after driving, the temperature gauge creeps up, or the oil looks milky. Later the check engine light may flash from a misfire.
issues.why: The lower intake manifold gaskets on the 3.1L V6 break down with age and heat. Coolant leaks outside the engine or into the oil. It is the most reported problem on this car, and some owners needed the repair more than once.
issues.next: Keep the coolant full and watch the temperature gauge. If it climbs, pull over and turn the engine off. Have a shop pressure-test the cooling system and check the oil for coolant, and fix it before coolant damages the engine bearings.

issues.t: Won't start with the security light on (Passlock)
issues.sym: The engine cranks but won't catch, or it starts and dies, and the anti-theft or security light comes on or flashes. Often it will start again after waiting 10 to 20 minutes.
issues.why: The anti-theft system in the ignition lock cylinder stops seeing the right signal and cuts fuel, thinking the car is being stolen. A worn lock cylinder or sensor is the usual cause.
issues.next: Try leaving the key in On for about 10 minutes until the security light stops flashing, then turn it off and try again. Have a shop read the codes and test the lock cylinder and anti-theft sensor so it doesn't strand you again.

issues.t: Front brake rotors warp, causing vibration
issues.sym: The steering wheel or brake pedal shakes or pulses when you brake, especially from highway speed. Some owners say stops take longer. It often comes back soon after the rotors are resurfaced.
issues.why: Many owners report front rotors warping again and again, with pads wearing quickly. Dealers often resurfaced the rotors rather than replacing them, and the problem returned.
issues.next: Have the brakes inspected if they pulse or stopping feels weaker. Replacing the rotors with good-quality new ones and having the wheel lug nuts tightened to spec usually works better than repeated resurfacing.

issues.t: ABS light comes on over bumps or in turns
issues.sym: The ABS warning light comes on or flashes, often after hitting a bump or turning, and may go out after restarting. ABS may kick in when it shouldn't.
issues.why: Front wheel speed sensors and their wiring are the usual suspects. Some owners had sensors replaced several times before the light stayed off.
issues.next: Your regular brakes normally still work with the ABS light on, but ABS may not, so leave extra stopping room. If the red brake light comes on or the pedal feels soft, stop driving and have it checked. Have the ABS codes read to find which sensor is at fault.

issues.sym: Steering gets heavy, like power steering has failed, often worse when turning left. You may hear clunking or squeaking from the front.
issues.why: Retainer parts for a bearing inside the steering rack can break, letting the pinion shaft move. Steering then takes much more effort (recall 03V-527, which covered about 750,000 GM cars).
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Ask an Oldsmobile or Chevrolet dealer with your VIN whether the recall repair was done.

issues.t: Passenger wiper can stop working in snow (recall)
issues.sym: In snow or ice, the wipers stop moving or the passenger-side wiper stops partway.
issues.why: Snow or ice can hold back the passenger wiper arm until the pivot housing cracks, and then the wipers stop (recall 01V-068).
issues.next: Clear snow and ice off the wipers before switching them on. Ask a dealer with your VIN whether the recall repair was done.

issues.t: Clunking or popping from the front end
issues.sym: A pop, clunk or rattle from the front when going over bumps or turning, sometimes with a ticking noise or vibration.
issues.why: Worn lower control arms or a worn or cracked steering rack were the common causes. Consumer Guide notes GM sometimes replaced the lower control arms or the rack for these noises, and one dealer found a broken weld on a rack.
issues.next: Have the front suspension and steering rack inspected soon, since a failing rack or control arm can affect steering. Also confirm the steering gear recall was done.

issues.t: Gas pedal hard to press (accelerator cable off the cam)
issues.sym: The accelerator pedal suddenly feels stiff or hard to push, and the engine doesn't respond normally.
issues.why: On 1997 cars the accelerator cable can slip off the throttle cam on the engine.
issues.next: If the pedal feels wrong, pull over safely and don't keep driving. Have a shop reseat or replace the throttle cable and check that the pedal returns freely.

issues.t: Key chime won't stop and power locks fail
issues.sym: The key-in-ignition chime keeps sounding after the key is removed, and the power door locks may stop working.
issues.why: A fault in the ignition lock cylinder keeps the system thinking the key is still in. Consumer Guide says the lock cylinder must be replaced.
issues.next: It isn't dangerous, but it can drain the battery and leave doors unlocked. Have the ignition lock cylinder replaced.

issues.sym: One door won't lock or unlock with the switch or remote, while the others work.
issues.why: A rubber part on the lock actuator arm inside the door can break.
issues.next: Lock that door by hand until it's fixed. Have the door lock actuator or the broken link replaced.

issues.t: Horn honks by itself or stops working
issues.sym: The horn goes off on its own, often in cold weather and sometimes in the middle of the night, or it doesn't sound when pressed.
issues.why: Owners blame an electrical fault in the horn circuit. A dealer told one owner the horn switch is part of the steering wheel airbag assembly, which makes the repair more involved.
issues.next: Pull the horn fuse or relay to stop a stuck horn until it's fixed. Because the horn switch sits with the airbag, have a qualified shop do the repair.

issues.sym: The A/C blows cold, then quits and won't come back on until you tap the temperature knob or restart the car.
issues.why: Owners report the A/C cutting out. One owner could bring it back by pressing the temperature knob, which points to a control or electrical fault; others ended up replacing the compressor.
issues.next: Have a shop check the refrigerant charge, compressor clutch and climate control before replacing the compressor.

issues.sym: The engine revs but the car doesn't pick up speed normally, shifts feel delayed, or gears seem to drop out.
issues.why: Internal wear in the 4-speed automatic. An owner reported needing a rebuild at about 88,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the transmission fluid level and condition. If it is slipping, avoid hard acceleration and get a diagnosis soon; driving on a slipping transmission makes the damage worse.

issues.sym: A tapping or ticking from the engine on cold mornings that fades as it warms up.
issues.why: Owners and shops haven't pinned down one cause. Low oil pressure at startup or valvetrain noise were suggested.
issues.next: Check the oil level and keep up with oil changes. If the noise gets louder, stays after warm-up, or the oil light flickers, have the oil pressure tested.

issues.sym: The turn signals stop flashing, or work only some of the time.
issues.why: The turn signal flasher relay fails. One owner needed two relays.
issues.next: Use hand signals until it's fixed. Replacing the flasher relay is usually a quick repair.

issues.sym: The radio suddenly gets only static or very weak stations.
issues.why: The antenna cable runs where a front passenger's foot can unplug it.
issues.next: Check the antenna cable connection behind the radio and on the passenger side. Plugging it back in and securing it usually fixes it.

issues.sym: The outside door handles on white cars turn yellow.
issues.why: Grease from the door lock cylinders stains the handles.
issues.next: This is cosmetic. Ask a dealer if anything remains of GM's past fix; otherwise new handles can be fitted.
